name: Haymarket meeting-site memorial

position.kind: OSM/Nominatim location lead, not approved public viewpoint

moment_title: Eight-hour organizing and the May 4 meeting
body: The Chicago History Museum connects the May 4, 1886 meeting with the eight-hour-day struggle and police violence at McCormick the previous day. The City’s landmark record locates the meeting area on Desplaines north of Randolph. The Illinois Labor History Society identifies Mary Brogger’s 2004 memorial at 175 North Desplaines. This is the Chicago meeting-site chapter, distinct from the cemetery monument in Forest Park. The bomber remains unidentified in the museum’s account; testimony and disputed details must retain their attribution.

name: Former criminal courthouse site / Courthouse Place exterior

position.kind: OSM/Nominatim location lead, not approved public viewpoint

moment_title: The trial site and the building that replaced it
body: The Haymarket trial took place in an earlier criminal courthouse at Hubbard and Dearborn. The museum’s account says that building was demolished in 1892 and replaced; the City lists today’s Courthouse Place as built in 1893. This exterior is an interpretation anchor for the changed site, not a surviving Haymarket courtroom or a pinpointed execution courtyard. The jail fabric also changed. Historical corner descriptions conflict in the inspected records, so no exact courtyard location is asserted. Current office entry is not part of this walking draft.
